note: CP-069 — the canonical ORDER-LIFECYCLE display contract, owned by PrepShip. Do not hand-edit: re-pin from upstream and let scripts/prepship-order-lifecycle-parity.mjs (rendered SQL + upstream blobs) and scripts/integration/client-portal-order-lifecycle-parity.ts (the REAL PrepShip functions, sibling checkout) prove the copy.
why: The Client Portal is a shadow renderer. A customer-facing 'Shipped' / 'Awaiting shipment' / 'Cancelled' / 'Voided' must come from the SAME evidence PrepShip's own Orders list, daily counts, dashboard and billing use — the effective-status CASE, the shipped-label display precedence and the active-outbound rule — never from carrier telemetry, tracking-number presence or the mere existence of a label row. PrepShip 0057 builds orders_effective_status_date_id_idx on the byte-identical CASE text, so the port must stay byte-identical for the shared production database to keep using that index.

effectiveStatusCase.normalisation: Both sides are compared after: CRLF -> LF; every whitespace run -> one space; trim. The pinned `source` / `aliasSource` texts are PrepShip's template literals exactly as its source spells them (`${orders.orderStatus}` / `${orderStatus}` interpolations). To compare a SOURCE template with RENDERED SQL, every column reference is reduced to its bare column name: `${orders.orderStatus}` and `${orderStatus}` -> order_status, `${orders.canonicalStatus}` and `${canonicalStatus}` -> canonical_status, `${orders.externallyShipped}` and `${externallyShipped}` -> externally_shipped; drizzle's rendered `"orders"."<column>"` -> <column>; an alias-qualified `<alias>.<column>` -> <column>. After that reduction the table form, the alias form and the rendered forms must all equal `canonical`.
effectiveStatusCase.source: case when lower(coalesce(${orders.orderStatus}, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(${orders.canonicalStatus}, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(${orders.orderStatus}, '')) = 'shipped' then 'shipped' when coalesce(${orders.externallyShipped}, false) = true then 'shipped' else coalesce(nullif(lower(${orders.orderStatus}), ''), 'awaiting_shipment') end
effectiveStatusCase.aliasSource: case when lower(coalesce(${orderStatus}, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(${canonicalStatus}, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(${orderStatus}, '')) = 'shipped' then 'shipped' when coalesce(${externallyShipped}, false) = true then 'shipped' else coalesce(nullif(lower(${orderStatus}), ''), 'awaiting_shipment') end
effectiveStatusCase.canonical: case when lower(coalesce(order_status, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(canonical_status, '')) = 'cancelled' then 'cancelled' when lower(coalesce(order_status, '')) = 'shipped' then 'shipped' when coalesce(externally_shipped, false) = true then 'shipped' else coalesce(nullif(lower(order_status), ''), 'awaiting_shipment') end

bucketPredicates.note: Orders tabs / counts render their WHERE on the INNER effective CASE (never on the wrapping bucket CASE). The shipped / cancelled equalities are served by PS 0057's expression index; the pending predicate is the complement (a negation a btree cannot serve) by design, so the tab and the badge can never disagree — admin-scope awaiting counts scan their scope, client-scoped callers use the client_id indexes. `{effective}` is the canonical CASE above.

shippedLabelDisplayState.gate: Evaluated ONLY where PrepShip evaluates it: inside resolveOrderLifecycleStatus's `orderStatus === 'shipped'` branch (order-lifecycle-status.ts:93-165), AFTER the canonical_status confirmation_failed / shipped_pending_confirmation checks. So an externally_shipped order that is not locally shipped, or a shipped order whose confirmation is pending/failed, is 'externally_shipped' / 'shipped_pending_confirmation' / 'confirmation_failed' (all → shipped) even with voided-only rows; the portal's order-status.ts mirrors that gate before calling resolveShippedLabelDisplayState (the sibling parity lane proves it over 1,680 cells).

activeOutboundPredicate.rule: voided = false AND is_return = false — returns and voided labels are never active outbound evidence (PrepShip shipment-aggregate.ts activeOutboundShipmentPredicate).
activeOutboundPredicate.portalListAdmissionNote: outboundShipmentPredicate() is the customer LIST admission (Shipments list + count, GET /orders/:id/shipments). voided is applied per surface (hidden unless ?status=voided) and is therefore not part of this fragment; is_return is PrepShip's arm; source <> 'replacement' is deviation D2 below.

projection.note: PrepShip OrderLifecycleStatus (resolveOrderLifecycleStatus().orderLifecycleStatus) -> Client Portal PortalOrderFulfillmentStatus. Every one of PrepShip's twelve statuses must appear here; scripts/integration/client-portal-order-lifecycle-parity.ts asserts portal.resolveOrderFulfillmentStatus(matrix) === this[PS.resolveOrderLifecycleStatus(matrix)].

deviations.what: Every order-grain shipment subquery (hasActiveOutboundShipment, hasVoidedOutboundShipment, displayTrackingNumber, carrier for trackingUrl) excludes coalesce(is_return, false) = true rows through the one shared fragment orderOutboundShipmentMatchSql.
deviations.prepship: shipment-aggregate.ts activeOutboundShipmentPredicate says the same (voided = false AND is_return = false), but routes/orders.ts (list query, ~1485-1516) picks the display `ship` row WITHOUT an is_return clause.
deviations.portal: Follows the named aggregate owner. An order whose only non-voided row is a return label reads 'Voided' here and 'Shipped' in PrepShip's list — rare; PrepShip follow-up filed.
deviations.surfaces: all order-grain subqueries + both outbound list surfaces

deviations.what: coalesce(source, '') <> 'replacement' is applied on customer LIST surfaces only (listPortalShipments list + count, GET /orders/:id/shipments) via outboundShipmentPredicate().
deviations.portal: Replacement vessels are orderless ('<n>-REPLACE', order_id NULL, source='replacement') and belong to the Replace surface (CP-061); they must never render as an 'Unavailable' outbound parcel. NOT in the order-grain match (documented no-op: such rows never match an order).

deviations.what: For shipments.order_id IS NULL rows the order_number fallback is scoped to the same client_id and prefers an effective-shipped order before newest id.
deviations.prepship: The orphan linker (order-sync.ts ~330-360) is unscoped and prefers a shipped order.
deviations.portal: Multi-tenant: two clients can share an order number, so cross-client rows resolve to 'unavailable' rather than another tenant's order. Walmart-direct duplicates within one client keep PrepShip's shipped-first preference. Consequence: PrepShip-unattributed labels (shipment-sync PS-467 rows with order_id NULL AND client_id NULL) never match — they read 'unavailable' for a global scope, are invisible to client scopes, and never promote an order or lend it a tracking number, whereas PrepShip's operator list attaches them by order_number alone. Attribution is PrepShip's to fix (stamp client_id / relink), not a portal inference.

deviations.prepship: PS-489 feeds hasExternalShipment so an active external-fulfillment RECORD reads 'external_label' instead of 'active_label'.
deviations.portal: Output-irrelevant: external_label and active_label both project to the customer word 'shipped'. The precedence itself is ported verbatim, including that arm.

deviations.what: The customer bucket 'pending' is the COMPLEMENT of the terminal two: awaiting_shipment, on_hold, awaiting_payment, pending_fulfillment and anything else PrepShip has not shipped or cancelled.
deviations.prepship: Files on_hold / awaiting_payment / pending_fulfillment under their own operator lifecycle statuses (projection table above maps them to pending).
deviations.portal: Awaiting + Shipped + Cancelled = All; a row can never sit in a tab that contradicts its badge. If DJ wants PrepShip's operator buckets, add 'on_hold' to the DTO enum.
deviations.surfaces: Orders badge, tabs, awaiting count, Analysis is_awaiting_order

deviations.what: The Awaiting tab additionally applies the portal's own visibleAwaitingOrdersPredicate (SEAuto / empty-placeholder suppression).
deviations.portal: PrepShip's eBay rule is NOT ported; the portal rule is stated as its own, not claimed as parity.

deviations.prepship: The lifecycle CASE has no such arms; Walmart 'canceled' is normalised to 'cancelled' before write; no writer of 'refunded' exists.
deviations.portal: Such spellings bucket as pending exactly as PrepShip does (0 rows in prod). buildCostSummary's refund money label in dto.ts is presentation, not a status owner.

deviations.what: 'voided' is rendered only when the effective status is 'shipped' AND the display state is voided_label. An awaiting order with voided-only rows renders 'pending'.
deviations.prepship: decideShipmentVoidLifecycle (shipment-aggregate.ts ~128-133) reopens an order to awaiting_shipment when its last active outbound label is voided; the PS-486 terminal-preserved population stays shipped.
deviations.portal: Correct only because PrepShip reopens: the portal depends on that write and never re-derives it. Today's ungated hasVoided && !hasActive -> voided mislabelled reopened orders.
